screening_results.reason: No emotion regulation instruction reported (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation results). Exclusion criteria met: none. Therefore excluded because participants viewed stimuli without performing a defined emotion-regulation task required for the review.

Task-based fMRI in depressed patients performing intentional emotion-introspection to down-regulate unpleasant affect, with task-related brain activation reported (amygdala, insula, PFC). Unclear from abstract whether regulation was applied to visual stimuli, so include for full-text review to resolve this.

Excluded because the study examined internal self-referential awareness/introspection (no mention of regulating responses to externally presented visual stimuli), which does not meet the review objective. Inclusion met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (emotion regulation of responses to visual stimuli or comparable reappraisal of visual stimuli). Exclusion criteria E1/E2 not met.

Included for full-text review because abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in human participants with PTSD and controls (I1, I3) and reports task-related brain activation (I4). It is unclear whether the 'emotional conflict task' required explicit emotion regulation (I2 not demonstrated); no exclusion criteria are met. Full text needed to confirm whether the task involves explicit regulation or passive viewing.

This is a resting-state fMRI connectivity study in women with PMDD (not a task-based study). It therefore does not meet I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), or I4 (task-related activation results). It does meet I3 (human clinical participants with a control group). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) are met. Excluded on basis of not satisfying core task-based inclusion criteria; high confidence from abstract.

Abstract reports comparisons of gambling disorder patients and healthy controls using brain activation measures of emotion regulation, indicating a task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation in human participants. Include for full-text review to confirm task specifics and contrasts.

fMRI study examining neural substrates of emotion regulation in women with PMDD; abstract implies a task probing emotion regulation but does not specify stimuli type, regulation instructions, or presence of a control group. Insufficient detail to confirm all inclusion criteria (especially I2 and I4), so include for full-text review.

Abstract reports comparison of reappraisal and acceptance as emotion regulation strategies applied to negative self-beliefs in social anxiety disorder (human clinical participants), but does not explicitly state task-based fMRI, report of task-related activations, or use of visual stimuli. Full text needed to confirm fMRI task and brain activation results.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study including an explicit cognitive emotion regulation task and an emotional Stroop, includes patient and control groups, and reports task-related brain activation (left supramarginal gyrus). No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review.

Abstract indicates a study of neural activation during emotion regulation in adolescents with and without suicidal ideation, but does not specify stimulus modality (visual) or full task details. Inclusion uncertain from abstract-only evidence, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI where participants ignored task-irrelevant unpleasant words (emotional interference), representing cognitive control of emotion/emotion regulation; includes non-patient groups (high AP/AR/AD and controls) and reports task-related functional connectivity results. All inclusion criteria I1–I4 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract describes a task-based functional neuroimaging study investigating behavioral and neural responses during emotion processing and regulation in OCD patients, unaffected siblings, and controls, and implies reporting of task-related brain activation. No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the task used auditory stimuli (laughter perception), not visual stimuli required by the meta-analysis objective. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I2, I3, I4. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criterion not demonstrated for this review: regulation of emotional response to visual stimuli (meta-analysis objective).

Abstract reports a task-based rt-fMRI study in humans training emotion regulation using a 'reality check' strategy during presentation of emotional pictures, includes healthy participants and a control group, and reports task-related activation and connectivity (amygdala down-regulation). No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in which human participants cognitively up-regulated (engaged) positive-social emotions from a first-person perspective and reports fMRI activation and effective connectivity results. This meets inclusion criteria I1–I4 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text review recommended to extract details.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise vs Look) in human patients with social anxiety disorder, and reports task-related brain activation predicting CBT outcome. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are indicated.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study examining emotion regulation and reports brain activation/connectivity in schizophrenia patients. It meets I1, I2, and I4. The abstract does not specify whether a separate control group was reported (I3 not demonstrated), but no exclusion criteria are met and information is insufficient to rule inclusion, so include for full-text review.

Excluded: the study used resting-state fMRI and did not involve a task-based emotion-regulation paradigm. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results). Confident the abstract lacks task-based emotion-regulation data and thus does not meet inclusion criteria.

Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) using visual stimuli (angry faces) in patients with depression and healthy controls; reports task-related neural activation (amygdala, insula, prefrontal regions). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports an empirical neurofeedback fMRI study in depressed and healthy adolescents targeting self-processing and emotion regulation, but it does not explicitly state a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation task with visual stimuli nor report task-related activation results. Include for full-text review to determine whether I1, I2, and I4 are met. I3 is clearly satisfied; no exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of human young adults performing cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) with task-related activation contrasts and results reported; does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full-text review appropriate to extract detailed activation data.

Study examines hippocampal subfield volumes in bipolar disorder related to childhood trauma (structural MRI); it is not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study and does not report task-related activation. Therefore does not meet I1, I2, or I4; I3 (human clinical participants) is met; no exclusion criteria apply.

Study investigates cognitive modulation of pain (pain attenuation strategies) rather than regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I2 (emotion regulation of visual stimuli) — reinterpretation targets pain, not emotional responses to visual stimuli. No exclusion criteria met.

Study uses resting-state fMRI, not a task-based emotion-regulation paradigm. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants with anxiety disorders and controls). Inclusion not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results). Exclusion criteria: none (E1,E2 not applicable).

Task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation (reappraisal/detachment) with passive viewing; includes clinical (AN) and age-matched control groups; reports behavioral arousal ratings and task-related fMRI activation results—meets all inclusion criteria.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I1); participants performed an implicit emotion regulation task (I2); includes clinical SAD group and healthy controls reported separately (I3); reports task-related brain activation/connectivity results (PPI amygdala-vmPFC) and pre/post treatment changes (I4). No exclusion criteria are met based on abstract.

Abstract investigates brain mechanisms in human BPD patients (clinical sample) but does not specify a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm or report task-related activation results. No exclusion criteria are met. Insufficient information to determine satisfaction of I1, I2, and I4, so include for full-text review.

Study used arterial spin labeling at rest to examine correlations between habitual emotion regulation and baseline rCBF; it did not involve a task-based fMRI emotion regulation paradigm or report task-related activation. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) with clinical participants (GAD and PD) and reports task-related brain activations predicting CBT response. No exclusion criteria are met and inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This study reports associations between subclinical symptoms and brain structure in a non-clinical sample (structural imaging), not a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human healthy participants). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract addresses volitional emotion regulation in anxiety and depression and references reappraisal-related neural substrates and case-control patient findings, but does not explicitly state task-based fMRI or report task activation results. Insufficient info to confirm I1 and I4, so include for full-text review.

The abstract describes a task-based fMRI study examining emotional reactivity and regulation in PTSD patients and links brain activation to treatment outcome. This meets inclusion criteria I1-I4. No exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract. Visual-stimulus specifics are not explicit but the study aligns with emotion regulation constructs relevant to the review.

This study used resting-state fMRI and diffusion tractography and assessed dispositional emotion regulation via questionnaire rather than a task during scanning. Therefore it does not meet I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), nor I4 (reports task-related activation). It does meet I3 (human clinical and control groups). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

This is a resting-state fMRI study with no task-based emotion regulation; no task-related activation results are reported. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation).

EXCLUDED: Study used EEG/ERP, not task-based fMRI (I1 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (self-focused cognitive reappraisal), I3 (human female participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation via ERPs). No exclusion criteria met (none).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive emotion regulation, reporting temporal dynamics of brain activation in bipolar disorder and schizophrenia. It meets I1, I2 and I4. It is unclear from the abstract whether a separate control group is reported (I3) and whether stimuli were visual and included view-without-regulate conditions, so full-text review is needed to confirm these points.

Task-based fMRI fear conditioning/extinction protocol constitutes a task involving viewing emotional (fear) stimuli (without instructed regulation) and reports task-related brain activation in human participants. Meets I1, I2 (viewing emotional stimuli/adjacent regulation domain), I3, and I4. No exclusion criteria met (not a non-empirical paper, not an empathy/perspective-taking study). Include for full-text review to confirm task details.

Excluded because the study uses resting-state fMRI acquired before and after an emotion-regulation task rather than reporting task-based fMRI activation; therefore I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (task-related activation results) are not met. It meets I2 (participants performed an emotion regulation task) and I3 (clinical and control groups). No exclusion criteria apply.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria I1, I3, I4 appear satisfied (task-based fMRI; clinical BPD sample; reports activation/connectivity). Inclusion criterion I2 (emotion regulation task) is not met or demonstrated: the study examines anger/aggression during script-driven provocation rather than participants applying an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal) or regulating responses to visual stimuli. Therefore exclude based on I2 not met.

Study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing cognitive reappraisal (watch vs reappraise) with clinical (SAD) and healthy control groups, and reports task-related brain activation/connectivity results. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of effortful emotion regulation (reappraisal) in bipolar disorder and reports altered prefrontal–amygdala effective connectivity. It meets I1, I2, and I4. Presence of a separate control group (I3) is not clearly stated, so include for full-text review.

E2 met: study uses Theory-of-Mind/perspective-taking processing without instruction to amplify or dampen emotion. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical and control groups). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no emotion-regulation task), I4 (reports connectivity rather than explicit task-related activation results).

Task-based rtfMRI neurofeedback study in human combat veterans performing emotion regulation (positive autobiographical recall); reports task-related brain activation mediators and includes experimental and control groups. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract does not specify task-based fMRI, an emotion regulation task, or use of visual stimuli; it refers to olfactory emotion induction in schizophrenia (human participants). Key inclusion criteria (I1, I2, I4) cannot be confirmed from the abstract, so include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

This is a structural MRI study reporting cortical thickness/subcortical volumes and self-report measures of affect; it does not report task-based fMRI, an emotion regulation task, or task-related brain activation. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met: I1, I2, I4. No exclusion criteria met (E1,E2).

Excluded because the abstract does not describe an emotion-regulation task. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion IDs not met: I2 (no instructions to regulate during the fMRI task; only passive viewing of sad faces and questionnaire measures of suppression). Therefore it fails the requirement that participants perform a task-based emotion-regulation procedure.

Task-based fMRI with human participants; participants were instructed to ignore emotional expressions while attending to face identity (fits cognitive control of emotion/attenuation), and the study reports task-related neural (functional connectivity) results. No exclusion criteria evident. Include for full-text review to confirm emotion-regulation framing.

Abstract indicates an empirical task-based fMRI study examining emotional reactivity and regulation in generalized anxiety disorder, reporting frontolimbic (prefrontal and amygdala) engagement. This fits I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I3 (clinical human participants), and I4 (task-related brain activation reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to confirm methods and control group details.

No exclusion criteria met. Excluded because the study uses resting-state fMRI (no task): it does not meet I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), or I4 (reports task-related activation). It does meet I3 (human participants of relevant ages). Based on the abstract, exclusion is clear.

Excluded because the abstract reports task-based fMRI (I1), human participants (I3), and task-related brain activation results (I4), but does not indicate an emotion-regulation task or instructions to modulate emotional responses (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria met (E1/E2 not applicable).

Task-based fMRI study where participants with GAD performed explicit emotion regulation (acceptance, worry, suppression) and the abstract reports task-related brain activations and connectivity. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I2, I4. The abstract does not state whether a separate control group was included, so I3 is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria met. Recommend full-text review to confirm sample/comparison details.

Task-based fMRI with participants viewing dental-treatment images that evoke fear/pain; reports task-related activation and connectivity in clinical and control groups. Abstract does not clearly state whether participants were instructed to regulate emotion (insufficient information). Because the review accepts studies that either regulate or simply view visual emotional stimuli, include for full-text review to confirm whether it meets the regulation-specific criteria.

Excluded: the study is a DTI structural MRI comparison in BPD vs controls, not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical and control groups reported). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI study), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). Confidence high because the abstract clearly describes diffusion MRI measures rather than task-evoked fMRI activation.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation paradigm in human participants (regular marijuana users and matched controls) and reports task-related brain activation results (amygdala, prefrontal networks). No exclusion criteria appear to apply.

Excluded because the study used resting-state fMRI (rs-FC) rather than a task-based emotion regulation paradigm and did not report task-related activation. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation). Exclusion criteria met: none.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI, uses distraction as an emotion regulation strategy, involves human clinical and control groups, and reports task-related neural activation results. No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to extract detailed ROI/contrast data.

Abstract reports an effective connectivity fMRI study in bipolar patients (human clinical sample: I3). However it does not specify a task-based fMRI emotion regulation or viewing paradigm, nor report task-related activation results (I1, I2, I4 not demonstrated). Insufficient information to judge inclusion on task/emotion-regulation criteria, so include for full-text review.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion I3 met (human clinical sample: North Korean refugees). Inclusion I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), and I4 (task-related brain activation results) are not met: study reports resting-state amygdala functional connectivity, not a task-based emotion regulation fMRI with task activations.

Study is a task-based fMRI with clinical and control groups and reports task-related brain activation. The abstract does not indicate participants were instructed to regulate emotions; stimuli were task-irrelevant and processed incidentally. Because it’s unclear whether this meets the review’s emotion-regulation or passive-viewing inclusion, include for full-text review to confirm.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I1) of cognitive reappraisal emotion regulation (I2) in human clinical (ASD) and control participants (I3), reporting task-related brain activation results (I4). No exclusion criteria evident.

Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal of aversive visual stimuli in human participants; reports task-related brain activation (amygdala, LPFC) and between-group comparison with/without neurofeedback. Meets all inclusion criteria; no exclusion criteria evident.

Abstract does not specify a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm or report task-related brain activation results, but studies adults (human participants). Insufficient information to determine inclusion, so include for full-text review.

Study is a task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in human clinical (GAD, PD) and healthy control groups and reports brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in human participants performing an emotion regulation task (veterans with PTSD and controls), and reports task-related brain activation results (PFC, SMA changes). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to extract detailed task contrasts and results.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study assessing the influence of induced emotions on a cognitive task, indicating I1 and I4 are met. It does not specify that participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 not demonstrated). Insufficient detail to determine regulation task presence, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI with human participants viewing emotionally salient child videos; reports task-related brain activation. Abstract does not state explicit emotion-regulation instructions, but the review includes studies that merely view visual emotional stimuli without regulating, so inclusion is uncertain from abstract alone — include for full-text review.

No evidence of a task-based emotion-regulation fMRI paradigm. Abstract describes functional dysconnectivity/connectivity in psychotic bipolar disorder (likely resting-state or connectivity analysis), not task activation. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results); I3 (participant/control group) not demonstrated in abstract.

Abstract reports a human trial teaching cognitive reappraisal to alter neural (reward/inhibitory region) responses to high-fat/high-sugar foods, meeting I2 (emotion regulation/cognitive reappraisal) and I3 (human participants). The abstract does not explicitly state task-based fMRI (I1) or clearly report task-related brain activation results (I4), so full-text review is needed to confirm fMRI and activation reporting.

Task-based fMRI in human participants with alcohol use disorder examining cognitive regulation of craving and negative emotion, reporting PFC recruitment and neural mechanisms (task-related brain activation). Meets I1, I2, I3, I4; no exclusion criteria apparent.

Abstract reports investigation of neural correlates of emotion regulation in human participants (twins), satisfying I2 (emotion regulation task) and I3 (human participants). The abstract does not explicitly state use of task-based fMRI or report task-related activation results, so inclusion on abstract alone is uncertain; include for full-text review to confirm I1 and I4.

Abstract examines distraction and reappraisal (emotion regulation) in remitted bipolar and unipolar patients and aims to compare context-dependent network interactions in the brain—consistent with the review topic. The abstract does not explicitly state the imaging modality or whether a separate control group and task-activation results are reported, so include for full-text review to confirm fMRI and reporting details.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of cognitive downregulation of negative/stressful sensations (emotion regulation), in human participants, and describes task-related brain activation results. Unclear whether stimuli were visual images specifically, so include for full-text review to confirm applicability to visual-stimulus meta-analysis.

Abstract addresses neural correlates of negative emotions and emotion regulation during anticipation of difficult tasks, but it does not explicitly state that task-based fMRI was used, whether participants were instructed to regulate emotions (vs. natural responses), or report task-related brain activation results. Insufficient information to confirm inclusion criteria from abstract alone; include for full-text review.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in human children (clinical MDD history and controls) and reports task-related functional connectivity results; no exclusion criteria met.

No evidence participants performed an emotion-regulation task (I2 not met). Abstract describes passive viewing and rating of aversive/neutral scenes; reports task fMRI activations (I1, I4) in clinical and control groups (I3). No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI with human participants (OD/BPD and healthy controls) performing an oddball task requiring attention amid negative emotional distractors (interpretable as cognitive control of emotion/affective regulation), and reporting task-related activation differences. No exclusion criteria met.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none (I3 not demonstrated in abstract). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not task-based; study is resting-state fMRI), I2 (no emotion-regulation task reported), I4 (no task-related activation results reported). Study does not address task-based emotion regulation with visual stimuli, so excluded.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI of humans (young adult smokers) performing an emotion-regulation (distancing) task with visual cues; reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria met.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI of emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal and distraction), healthy human participants, and reports task-related BOLD activation results. No exclusion criteria are met.

No exclusion criteria were met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activation/validation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 — abstract does not describe an emotion-regulation task (e.g., cognitive reappraisal or instructed regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli); it focuses on DMN modulation/neurofeedback and DMN activation/deactivation tasks.

Patient-only fMRI neurofeedback study (Patients n=10) with no separately reported control group in the abstract. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performed an emotion regulation task—downregulation while viewing trauma words), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met/not demonstrated: I3 (no control group reported for the patient sample). Exclusion criteria: none met (E1,E2 not applicable).

Task-based fMRI study examining voluntary attentional regulation of emotion (an emotion regulation strategy) and emotion recognition in depressed patients and controls; reports activation and connectivity results. Fits meta-analysis objective and meets inclusion criteria I1-I4. No exclusion criteria met.

Study addresses emotion circuitry and regulation in human first-degree relatives but abstract does not specify whether a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation (view vs regulate) paradigm was used or whether task-related activation results are reported. Insufficient information to confirm I1, I2, and I4, but I3 (human participants) is met. Include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

The study used an emotion-word Stroop to probe selective attention to emotional distraction, not an explicit emotion-regulation task (no instructions to up-/down-regulate or reappraise). Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human adult sample), I4 (task-related activation reported). Inclusion not met: I2 (emotion regulation task). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports an emotion regulation task comparing brain activation across schizophrenia patients, non-affected siblings, and healthy controls, and thus addresses the review objective. It does not explicitly state fMRI or stimulus modality (visual) in the abstract, so full text is needed to confirm imaging modality and stimulus type. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract lacks key details: it does not state whether task-based fMRI was used, whether participants performed an explicit emotion regulation task, or whether task-related brain activation results are reported. Because inclusion cannot be determined from the abstract alone, include for full-text review to assess I1–I4.

Study reports fMRI work in human clinical participants (children with ASD) but the abstract does not specify a task-based emotion-regulation or passive viewing paradigm nor explicitly report task-related activation results. No exclusion criteria are met. Insufficient information to determine eligibility from abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal in adult human participants that reports task-related brain activation (PFC and amygdala). The abstract meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are apparent, so include for full-text review.

EXCLUDED: Study uses resting-state fMRI rather than a task-based emotion-regulation paradigm. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants; patient group with controls). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion-regulation task), I4 (no task-related activation results).

Task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation (worry induction and worry reappraisal) in late-life GAD reporting functional connectivity results; meets I1, I2, I3, and I4. No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to confirm sample/control details and task contrasts.

No evidence the task was an emotion-regulation task: fMRI compared scratching/picking vs caressing (tactile stimulation) rather than instructed regulation of emotional responses to stimuli. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical sample with control group), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (no demonstrated emotion-regulation instructions or paradigm). Exclusion criteria: none met.

Excluded because the study is a single-arm patient trial with no separate control group (I3 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI neurofeedback), I2 (participants performed an emotion-regulation task: amygdala downregulation), I4 (reports task-related BOLD/amygdala activation). Exclusion criteria met: none (E: []).

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI not stated in abstract), I2 (no evidence participants performed an emotion-regulation task on visual stimuli—study involves mood induction and pain), I4 (task-related brain activation results not reported in abstract). Therefore excluded from this review.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I2 (emotion regulation task with Maintain/Reappraise) and I3 (human SAD and control groups). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study — EEG study) and I4 (does not report task-related fMRI activation results). Therefore exclude.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study investigating emotion regulation in ADHD, matching the review objective. However, it does not specify whether a separate control group was reported or explicitly state task-related activation results in the abstract. Include for full-text review to confirm control group reporting and reported activation results.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human clinical and control groups reported). Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study; uses structural MRI/gray matter volume), I2 (participants did not perform an emotion regulation task), I4 (does not report task-related brain activation results). Therefore excluded based on failure to meet required inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I4.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study examining volitional emotion regulation in veterans with PTSD and reports neural activation results. It does not clearly state whether a separate control group is included, so include for full-text review to confirm eligibility.

Task-based fMRI in human children/adolescents reporting task-related amygdala-prefrontal activation/connectivity and behavioral regulation. Abstract does not specify explicit instructed emotion-regulation strategy, but the study fits the review objective of viewing visual (maternal) stimuli that modulate emotion-related circuitry; inclusion of viewing-without-regulating studies is allowed. Full text needed to confirm task details and contrast definitions.

Abstract reports fMRI classification of MDD vs BD in medication-free subjects but does not specify a task or that participants performed an emotion regulation or emotional viewing task, nor report task-related activation. No exclusion criteria are met. Insufficient information to determine inclusion; include for full-text review.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study comparing cognitive reappraisal and placebo emotion regulation, reports neural activation changes (amygdala, insula, PFC, subgenual cingulate), and involves human participants performing emotion regulation. Meets inclusion criteria I1–I4, and no exclusion criteria are evident. Include for full-text review to confirm details.

Study reports resting-state functional connectivity in bipolar disorder, not a task-based fMRI emotion regulation study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (no task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion regulation task), I4 (no task-related activation reported).

Exclude: study reports resting-state cerebellar-cerebral functional connectivity in OCD, not a task-based emotion regulation paradigm. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical sample). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results).

Study used structural (anatomical) MRI to measure dACC volume and trait emotion-regulation measures, not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (healthy human participants). Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation).

Abstract reports a task-based human fMRI study where participants used cognitive reappraisal to decrease negative emotions induced by bottom-up and top-down generation; neural (amygdala) and self-report results are reported, matching inclusion criteria for task fMRI, emotion regulation, participant groups, and task-related brain activation.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study with human participants performing an active cognitive emotion regulation task (cognitive reappraisal), includes both depressed patients and healthy controls, and reports whole-brain activation and connectivity results relevant to regulation vs. passive viewing; meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract provides insufficient methodological detail to confirm inclusion: it does not state whether task-based fMRI was used, whether participants performed an instructed emotion-regulation task during fMRI, or whether task-related brain activation results are reported. No exclusion criteria are met in the abstract. Include for full-text review to assess I1–I4.

Abstract addresses emotion regulation differences between MDD and BD but does not specify use of task-based fMRI, an emotion-regulation task, or task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met. Because inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone, include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain connectivity/activation results). Inclusion not met: I2 — study uses a psychosocial stress induction (Montreal Imaging Stress Task) and examines stress reactivity/brain network efficiency, not an emotion regulation task (e.g., reappraisal or instructed regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli). Therefore excluded.

This is a resting-state fMRI study (no task). The abstract does not describe a task-based emotion regulation or viewing task, nor task-related activation results. Exclusion criteria: none met. Inclusion criteria met: none demonstrated. Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation/viewing task), I4 (task-related brain activation results); I3 (participant/control group) not demonstrated in abstract.

Task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal to regulate negative emotions and reporting neuronal correlates in borderline patients. Abstract does not clearly state whether a separate control group is reported, so full text needed to confirm I3. Include for full-text review.

The study examines regulation of negative autobiographical memories (internal recall), not regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli required by the review objective. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I2, I3, I4. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: none.

Abstract/title do not specify whether this is a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study nor whether task-related brain activation results are reported. No exclusion criteria are evident. Insufficient information to determine inclusion from abstract alone — include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI investigating emotional conflict and reports fronto-limbic activity/connectivity (meets I1 and I4). Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal in human participants (low vs high externalizing psychopathology) reporting task-related brain activation (amygdala, parietal, occipital). Meets I1-I4 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Include for full-text review.

Study uses resting-state fMRI and examines amygdala functional connectivity in PTSD, not a task-based emotion regulation or viewing task and does not report task-related activations. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion not met: I1, I2, I4. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports an fMRI study in bipolar patients (clinical human sample) but does not specify a task-based emotion-regulation paradigm or clearly report task-related activation to emotional visual stimuli. Because inclusion status is uncertain from the abstract and no exclusion criteria are met, include for full-text review to determine whether I1, I2 and I4 are satisfied.

Excluded because participants did not perform an emotion regulation task (I2 not met): they viewed emotional faces and made perceptual judgments without instruction to regulate. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human children sample), I4 (reports task-related activation). No exclusion criteria met.

No exclusion criteria met. Human participants are included (I3 met). Not a task-based fMRI activation study—uses resting-state functional connectivity after script-driven imagery (I1 not met). No explicit emotion-regulation task described (I2 not met). Does not report task-related activation results (I4 not met).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans using an emotion regulation (reappraisal/maintain/suppress) task, includes clinical (cocaine+Cluster B) and control groups, and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results. Satisfies inclusion criteria; no exclusion criteria apparent from abstract.

No exclusion criteria met. The abstract reports cytokine and μ-opioid function in MDD and healthy volunteers but provides no evidence of a task-based fMRI, an emotion-regulation task, or task-related brain activation results. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants: MDD and healthy volunteers). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

Excluded because inclusion criterion I2 (emotion regulation task) is not met: abstract describes mood induction and reward/frustration responses but no instruction to regulate emotion (e.g., reappraisal). Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Exclusion criteria met: [].

Task-based fMRI with SZ and matched controls; reports task-related brain activation (left IFG) during emotional distractors and WM load. Abstract does not clearly state whether participants were explicitly instructed to regulate emotions (regulation vs. passive ignoring of distractors is ambiguous). Include for full-text review to determine whether I2 (emotion regulation task) is met.

Task-based fMRI study of human participants performing cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation). Abstract reports task-related brain activation results (amygdala, prefrontal) during regulation. No exclusion criteria met.

Exclusion based on study using voxel-based structural MRI (VBM) rather than task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigms. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). No exclusion criteria from E1–E2 apply.

Exclusion: No exclusion criteria met (E1,E2). Inclusion: Human participants present (I3 met). Not eligible because it is not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met), does not involve an emotion-regulation task (I2 not met), and does not report task-related brain activation results (I4 not met). This is a DTI structural connectivity study predicting trait anxiety, outside the review's fMRI emotion-regulation scope.

Abstract reports an fMRI study in anorexia nervosa showing activation changes to intimate stimuli, but does not state whether the task involved explicit emotion regulation or passive viewing; insufficient detail to confirm I1 and I2 from abstract alone. Include for full-text review to confirm task design and emotion-regulation instructions.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion I3 met (human postpartum participants). Inclusion I1 not met (resting-state, not task-based fMRI), I2 not met (no emotion regulation task; resting connectivity only), I4 not met (reports resting-state connectivity, not task-related activation). Therefore excluded for not meeting core task-based emotion-regulation study criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of human youth viewing emotional (negative) faces vs shapes (implicit emotion processing), reports task-related brain activation and includes clinical and control groups; the meta-analysis objective explicitly admits studies that view emotional stimuli without regulation, so the study is eligible for full-text review.

This is a structural MRI (voxel/region-based morphometry) study of brain volumes in offender groups, not a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3. Inclusion IDs not met: I1, I2, I4.

Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal applied to anticipatory anxiety in human participants; reports task-related brain activation and correlations with subjective anxiety. Meets inclusion criteria I1-I4; no exclusion criteria apparent from abstract.

Abstract reports neural and behavioural responses during anticipatory fear in men with schizophrenia or APD (human clinical sample), but does not explicitly state task-based fMRI, an emotion-regulation instruction, or task-related activation results. I3 is clearly met; I1, I2, and I4 are not demonstrated in the abstract. Include for full-text review to confirm imaging and task details.

Abstract reports a randomized clinical trial in human patients with social anxiety disorder examining cognitive reappraisal (an emotion regulation task) and neural (prefrontal) responses. However the abstract does not explicitly confirm task-based fMRI, task-related activation results, or use of visual stimuli; full text needed to confirm I1 and I4 and stimulus modality.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in adult humans using instructed cognitive reappraisal (Social-Reg) versus look, reporting task-related brain activation contrasts and associations with behavior; meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are evident.

No exclusion criteria are met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human patient sample with a separately reported traumatized control group). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study; uses DTI structural imaging), I2 (no emotion regulation task), I4 (no task-related brain activation results reported).

No task-based fMRI or emotion-regulation task reported (SPECT used during mutism); not a task-based fMRI study and no task-related fMRI activation results. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met: I1, I2, I4. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a controlled fMRI study in patients with bipolar disorder, indicating human clinical participants with a control group (I3). However, it does not specify whether the fMRI was task-based, whether participants performed an emotion-regulation or visual-stimulus viewing task, or whether task-related activation results are reported (I1, I2, I4 unclear). Include for full-text review to determine task details and reported activations.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI emotion regulation study (amygdala neurofeedback during aversive-picture viewing) reporting task-related activation and connectivity, but it does not indicate whether a control group is reported for this clinical BPD sample (I3 not demonstrated). Include for full-text review to resolve this uncertainty.

Abstract does not report whether this is a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study or whether task-related activation contrasts meet inclusion criteria. Title suggests affect processing in methamphetamine dependence but provides insufficient detail. Include for full-text review to determine I1, I2, and I4.

Task-based fMRI study in humans (patients with SAD) where participants performed emotion regulation (reappraisal) of social evaluation and the paper reports task-related brain activation changes; meets I1-I4 and no exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Abstract examines neural correlates of emotion regulation in late-life GAD (human clinical sample). However, it does not specify use of a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm nor clearly report task-related activation in the abstract. Insufficient information to confirm I1 and I4, so include for full-text review.

EXCLUDE: Study uses resting-state fMRI rather than a task-based emotion regulation paradigm. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical participants with MDD). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation).

Study is a task-based fMRI with human PTSD and control groups and reports task-related activations (meets I1, I3, I4). However, participants only observed negative and neutral images without any instruction to regulate their emotions, so I2 (emotion regulation task) is not met. No exclusion criteria apply ( []).

E1 met: abstract describes conceptual/proposal paper on fMRI neurofeedback without reporting original human empirical data. No evidence of a task-based fMRI study or participants performing an emotion regulation task, nor task-related brain activation results. Inclusion criteria I1-I4 are not demonstrated and thus not met.

Task-based fMRI with human participants and task-related activation reported (I1, I3, I4). Abstract does not indicate participants engaged in an explicit emotion-regulation instruction (I2 uncertain), but the review objective allows passive viewing; abstract insufficient to determine definitively. Include for full-text review to clarify whether this study fits the regulation/viewing criteria.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of cognitive emotion regulation in previously depressed and healthy children, reporting neural activation differences during regulation. Meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, and I4; no exclusion criteria evident.

Exclusion: None (no exclusion criteria met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (no emotion regulation instruction—passive viewing of emotional faces). The study does not involve an instructed emotion-regulation task, so it is excluded.

Abstract describes an empirical task-based fMRI study in humans using cognitive reappraisal to regulate emotion, reports task-related brain activation results, and includes clinical and control groups. No exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because this is a structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) study comparing gray matter volumes, not a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion-regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation). High confidence.

Abstract describes passive processing of emotional words in a task-based fMRI study with healthy participants and reports task-related activation and connectivity. However, it does not report an instructed emotion-regulation task (only mentions possible 'unintentional' regulation). Therefore I2 (emotion regulation task) is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI in unmedicated depressed adults measuring pretreatment neural reactivity to emotional visual stimuli that predicts CBT response. This meets I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (clinical human participants), and I4 (reports task-related brain activation results). The abstract does not specify an explicit regulation instruction, but the review objective accepts viewing without regulating, so I2 is considered met. No exclusion criteria are identified from the abstract.

Excluded because the study is a structural MRI morphometry study, not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion-regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in human participants and presents amygdala activation results predicting anxiety (I1, I3, I4 met). However, it does not clearly state that participants performed an explicit emotion-regulation task (I2 not demonstrated). Because of this uncertainty, include for full-text review to verify whether an emotion-regulation or relevant viewing/regulation condition was used.

Study is a voxel-based morphometry (structural MRI) investigation of gray matter in depressed female outpatients; it is not a task-based fMRI study and does not report task-related brain activation during emotion regulation. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a fear-conditioning/generalization fMRI task without any instruction to regulate emotional responses. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion ID not met: I2 (no emotion-regulation task reported).

Task-based fMRI in humans reporting task-related activations (I1, I3, I4). Abstract does not clearly indicate an instructed emotion-regulation task or that participants performed regulation of visual stimuli (I2 not demonstrated); insufficient information to determine inclusion, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI using an emotional faces paradigm (viewing emotional stimuli without regulation is allowed by review). Human clinical older adult sample (late-life depression). Reports task-related functional activation. No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study using a Stroop Match-to-Sample with emotional (angry face) interference; examines prefrontal cognitive control over emotion and reports task-related activations and functional connectivity in adolescents with Internet gaming disorder and controls. Meets inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI, cognitive control of emotion, eligible participant groups, and reporting task-related brain activation. No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

This is an fMRI study using a re-appraisal emotion regulation task in human participants (cocaine-dependent and matched controls) and reports task-related activations and connectivity, meeting all inclusion criteria.

Abstract indicates a human clinical neuroimaging study of emotion processing in Takotsubo patients (satisfies I3) but does not specify a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm, nor report task-related activation results (I1, I2, I4 not demonstrated). Insufficient information to determine inclusion — include for full-text review.

Abstract provides insufficient information to determine whether a task-based emotion regulation paradigm was used or whether task-related activation results relevant to the meta-analysis are reported. It clearly involves human adolescent participants (I3). Include for full-text review to assess I1, I2, and I4.

Abstract studies human participants (bipolar patients and relatives) and neural processing of sad facial affect but does not specify use of task-based fMRI, an emotion-regulation instruction, or task-related activation results. Insufficient information to confirm I1, I2, or I4 from the abstract alone; include for full-text review.

No evidence this is a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation. The abstract describes altered structural/white-matter connectivity in GAD (likely DTI), not an emotion-regulation task or task-related activation. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation); I3 (human participants) is implied but control group not specified.

Study used resting-state functional connectivity in MDD patients and controls, not a task-based emotion regulation fMRI paradigm. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results). Exclusion criteria met: none (E1,E2 not applicable).

Task-based fMRI with human participants reporting task-related activation (I1, I3, I4) but the task (Prisoner’s Dilemma social interactions) does not involve instructed emotion regulation strategies; inclusion criterion I2 is not met. No exclusion criteria apply.

Task-based fMRI in human patients with SAD examining neural connectivity during affect labeling, so I1, I3 and I4 appear satisfied. The abstract does not clearly state that affect labeling here is an emotion-regulation task applied to visual stimuli (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to confirm whether affect labeling fits the review’s emotion-regulation/visual-stimulus requirements.

Task-based fMRI study of depressed and control participants performing reappraisal (detachment/immersion) with reported amygdala and prefrontal activation differences. Meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract; include for full-text review.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical participants with treatment-resistant depression). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results). The study reports resting-state fMRI connectivity predicting placebo response to sham rTMS, not a task-based emotion-regulation paradigm, so it does not meet the review’s task-based emotion-regulation inclusion criteria.

EXCLUDED because the study is structural morphometry (sulcal variability/volumetry) in healthy participants, not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human healthy participants). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

Patient-only sample with no separate control group reported, so inclusion criterion I3 is not met. The study is a task-based fMRI study (I1), uses emotion reactivity and regulation tasks (I2), and reports task-related activation results (I4). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) are met based on the abstract.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans (N=20) with task-related brain activation and healthy participants. It is unclear whether participants were instructed to regulate emotions (vs. passive viewing); therefore inclusion for full-text review is warranted to determine if the task meets the review's emotion-regulation criteria.

Study used resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) rather than a task-based paradigm. It does not involve an emotion-regulation task with visual stimuli or report task-related activation results. It includes human clinical participants (MDD) but fails I1, I2, and I4. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in clinical out-patients examining brain activation to emotional facial expressions (meets I1, I3, I4). It does not state whether participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria met. Abstract insufficient to determine regulation vs passive viewing; include for full-text review.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI of children using cognitive reappraisal to regulate emotional responses to visual (sad) stimuli, and reports task-related brain activation (PFC, amygdala). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation instruction). Recommend full-text review.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI regional responses, connectivity and habituation to emotional stimuli in female BPD participants, satisfying I1, I3, and I4. It does not state participants were instructed to regulate their emotions (I2 not demonstrated). Because viewing without regulating also fits the review objective and regulation status is unclear from the abstract, include for full-text review.

Abstract describes task-based fMRI with human participants and task-related activations, but does not involve an emotion-regulation instruction or strategy (e.g., reappraisal/acceptance) nor explicit regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli; therefore I2 not met. No exclusion criteria clearly apply.

Excluded because the study reports resting-state fMRI connectivity in veterans, not a task-based emotion-regulation or stimulus-viewing fMRI. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results). No exclusion criteria met (none of E1/E2 apply).

Task-based fMRI study in humans performing an explicit emotion regulation task (maintain/enhance/suppress) with patient (mTBI) and control groups and reporting task-related brain activation, meeting I1,I2,I3,I4; no exclusions met.

Abstract reports connectivity and treatment-response in major depression but does not describe a task-based emotion-regulation fMRI paradigm or task-related activation. Exclusion criteria: none met. Inclusion met: I3 (clinical participants). Inclusion not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation).

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion IDs not met: I2 (not an emotion regulation task; study reports appetitive conditioning without instructions to regulate emotional responses). The abstract does not describe any reappraisal/acceptance/distancing or other regulation instructions, so it does not meet the review objective.

Study uses resting-state fMRI rather than a task-based emotion regulation or viewing task. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participant groups: LTAA and NSAC). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related activation results).

E2 met: study is a mentalizing/Prisoner's Dilemma fMRI task without instruction to amplify or dampen participants' own emotional responses. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (not an emotion-regulation task).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans using emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and distraction) with remitted depressed patients and healthy controls, and reports task-related brain activation (amygdala, ACC, OFC). Meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are indicated.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study using an affect-labeling emotion-regulation task in human participants (social phobia groups and healthy controls) and reports task-related amygdala and prefrontal activation/connectivity; no exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the abstract reports a task-based fMRI cue-exposure study with alcoholic and social drinker groups and task-related activations (meets I1, I3, I4) but does not describe any emotion-regulation instructions (reappraisal, distancing, regulation during anticipation/cue) and appears to be passive cue-reactivity; therefore I2 is not met. No exclusion criteria are met (none).

Abstract indicates an fMRI study of mood-linked neural responses after a mood challenge in remitted depressed patients, but does not specify an emotion regulation task (e.g., reappraisal) or details of stimulus viewing/regulation. Inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI using the affective Stroop (cognitive control over emotional stimuli). Abstract reports task-related BOLD changes linked to emotional vs neutral/incongruent vs congruent stimuli in human trauma-exposed participants and examines neural correlates of symptom change. Meets I1, I2 (cognitive control of emotion), I3, and I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports an emotional go/no-go task in adolescents addressing neural substrates of emotional reactivity and regulation, but it does not clearly state whether an explicit emotion-regulation instruction or fMRI activation results are reported. Inclusion is uncertain from abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Study is a task-based fMRI investigation in human juvenile schizophrenia patients with reported task-related activations (I1, I3, I4 met). However, it uses an emotion discrimination/viewing task without any instruction to regulate or modulate emotional responses, so I2 (emotion regulation task) is not met. No exclusion criteria apply (none met).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of voluntary emotion regulation that reduces amygdala activation to aversive stimuli, indicating human participants performed an emotion regulation task and task-related brain activation was reported. No exclusion criteria are met from the abstract.

EXCLUDED: No evidence participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human adolescent participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Exclusion criteria met: none (E[]). The study used a social exclusion (Cyberball) paradigm assessing emotional responsivity, not an emotion regulation task.

This is a resting-state fMRI study of adolescent girls (no task or emotion-regulation paradigm). It therefore does not meet I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), or I4 (task-related activation results). I3 (human adolescent participants) is met. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

Abstract implies brain imaging with reported activation of emotion-regulation neurocircuits but does not specify whether participants performed an emotion regulation task or whether humans were tested. Insufficient information to confirm all inclusion criteria, so include for full-text review.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in depressed youth and healthy controls, and reports task-related brain activation (amygdala, vmPFC). This satisfies the review inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met from the abstract.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of neural responses to frustration in children, but does not specify an emotion-regulation instruction, whether stimuli were visual, whether a control group is reported, or provide task activation details. Insufficient information to confirm I2, I3, and I4, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study of implicit emotion processing (gender discrimination) in healthy human participants that reports task-related activation (amygdala BOLD response and functional connectivity) to emotional facial expressions. Although not an explicit regulation task, the meta-analysis includes passive viewing of emotional stimuli, so inclusion criterion for emotion-regulation/viewing is satisfied.

Abstract does not specify a task-based emotion-regulation fMRI paradigm or report task-related activation; it likely examines amygdala connectivity (possibly resting-state). Insufficient information to determine whether inclusion criteria I1-I4 are met; include for full-text review.

No emotion regulation instruction reported (I2 not met). Study is a task-based fMRI with human participants and reports task-related activations (I1, I3, I4 met). No exclusion criteria met. Abstract describes viewing and imagining images but not regulating emotion (reappraisal/acceptance/etc.), so it fails the emotion-regulation inclusion criterion.

fMRI study with task-based functional analyses of perceptual processing of fearful visual stimuli in healthy humans, reporting task-related activation and coupling. The abstract does not describe an emotion-regulation instruction (uncertain if passive viewing is eligible under review scope), so include for full-text review to determine whether it meets the regulation/viewing criteria.

Task-based fMRI study examining acceptance as an emotion-regulation strategy in individuals with BPD; reports neural correlates (brain activation). Fits inclusion criteria I1–I4 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Excluded: study is not a task-based fMRI study (uses FDG-PET) and does not involve an emotion-regulation task or report task-related activations; therefore I1, I2, and I4 are not met. It does include human clinical participants (I3 met). No exclusion criteria apply (E1/E2 not met).

The study does not manipulate or instruct emotion regulation (it used an emotional declarative memory/encoding task), so I2 (emotion regulation task) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (clinical group with controls), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria apply (E1,E2 not met).

No task-based fMRI or emotion regulation task reported. Inclusion met: I3 (human non-clinical sample). Inclusion not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

Task-based fMRI in humans viewing masked emotional (happy/fearful) faces; reports task-related activation differences in anterior cingulate and amygdala. Although participants passively viewed stimuli (no regulation instruction), the review includes studies that view emotional stimuli without regulating. Thus the abstract meets the review objective and reports task-related activation results, supporting inclusion for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI in healthy adult humans reporting task-related brain activation (ACC). The abstract does not specify that participants were instructed to perform an emotion regulation strategy (uncertain whether anticipation counts as regulation), so I2 is not demonstrated from abstract alone; include for full-text review to resolve.

Task-based fMRI study of angry face processing in healthy human participants reporting task-related brain activations. The abstract does not state whether participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 uncertain). No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to determine if the task involved explicit emotion regulation or qualifies as passive viewing per the review objective.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants with patient and control groups), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I2 — the study used a Monetary Incentive Delay task assessing reward/punishment processing, not an emotion-regulation task (no reappraisal/acceptance/instruction to regulate emotions).

Task-based fMRI study that used an emotion regulation paradigm asking participants to increase positive emotion; includes clinical (depressed) and healthy control groups and reports task-related brain activation/connectivity results (nucleus accumbens and fronto-striatal connectivity). All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluding because the study is a task-based fMRI study with clinical and control adolescent groups and reports task-related activations (I1, I3, I4 met). However, it does not describe an emotion-regulation task or instructions to amplify/dampen emotional responses (I2 not met). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical and control groups), I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion not met: I2 — this is a distress-tolerance PASAT task, not an emotion-regulation task involving instructed regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli; thus does not meet the meta-analysis’ emotion-regulation task criterion.

Study used structural (T1) MRI in healthy adults reporting hippocampal cell density. It is not a task-based fMRI study, does not involve an emotion-regulation task, and does not report task-related brain activation. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1, I2, I4.

EXCLUDE: Study uses resting-state fMRI (no task) and does not involve an emotion regulation task or report task-related activation. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants, adults and adolescents). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (participants did not perform an emotion-regulation task or were not instructed to regulate). Also study used auditory comments, not visual stimuli required by the review objective, so it does not address the review question.

E1 (non-empirical conceptual/review article): abstract describes a conceptual model and does not report original human task-based fMRI data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (human participants performing an emotion regulation task), I3 (participant groups reported), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

Abstract lacks sufficient detail to confirm I1 (task-based fMRI) and I2 (participants instructed to regulate emotion) or whether visual emotional stimuli were merely viewed; title suggests negative emotional distraction but task details and presence of control group are not reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

This is a task-based fMRI study reporting BOLD responses in phobic participants viewing phobia-related images, but the abstract does not describe any emotion-regulation instructions or strategies (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance). Inclusion criterion I2 (emotion regulation task) is not met, so the study is excluded.

Task-based fMRI study in humans reporting task-related brain activation during anticipation of emotional visual stimuli. Participants viewed (without explicit regulation) emotional pictures and anticipation was examined; fits meta-analysis objective of studies that regulate or view without regulating. Clinical and control groups reported separately. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in human patients performing an emotion regulation task (cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative affect), and reports task-related brain activation results. This satisfies inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI study examining neural circuitry supporting emotion regulation using an emotional n-back task in human clinical groups; reports task-related anterior cingulate activation distinguishing bipolar vs unipolar depressed females. Inclusion criteria I1, I3, and I4 are clearly met; I2 is reasonably met because the study targets emotion regulation circuitry and uses emotional stimuli (fits the review objective of regulation or viewing). No exclusion criteria apply.

E1: This is a protocol paper (no original human data or task results reported). Inclusion met: I3 (clinical human participants implied). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (no clear evidence of task-based fMRI), I2 (no explicit emotion-regulation task described), I4 (no task-related brain activation results reported).

No task-based emotion regulation paradigm reported: meets I3 (human clinical and control groups) but does NOT meet I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), or I4 (task-related activation results). No exclusion criteria met (none). Exclude because study is resting-state connectivity, not a task fMRI emotion-regulation study.

Abstract does not explicitly state task-based fMRI or that participants were instructed to regulate emotions, but it investigates neurobiological mechanisms of a positivity bias in older adults and reports anterior cingulate activation, indicating human participants and brain activation. Exclusion criteria not met. Insufficient information to confirm I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), and I4 (task-related activation reported) from abstract alone — include for full-text review.

Resting-state fMRI study without any task or emotion-regulation paradigm. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results).

Abstract reports task-based fMRI cue-exposure in alcohol-dependent humans examining brain activation to alcohol-related cues (fits task-based and cue viewing without regulation). Task-based fMRI study of human participants using guided cognitive reappraisal (creative reappraisal) to regulate negative emotion; reports task-related brain activation (amygdala, hippocampus, ventral striatum). No exclusion criteria met based on abstract.
