Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation).

This is a surgical study of microprolactinomas, not a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation; it does not report emotion regulation tasks or task-related brain activation. Inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I4 are not met. No exclusion criteria are met.

Not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study. Abstract describes intracerebral recordings in 3 epilepsy patients during seizures, with no fMRI, no emotion-regulation task, and no separate control group. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1, I2, I3, I4.

E1: Narrative review without original human data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study), I2 (not an emotion-regulation task), I3 (no relevant participant task group reported), I4 (no task-related brain activation results).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in healthy human participants examining expressive suppression (an emotion regulation strategy) with reported amygdala activation results; meets I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria are evident.

Title indicates emotion regulation in social anxiety disorder with behavioral and neural responses to socio-emotional tasks, consistent with emotion-regulation task and neural outcome; abstract does not explicitly state task-based fMRI methods, so inclusion cannot be confirmed from abstract alone. Include for full-text review to determine imaging modality and task details.

Structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) study of gray matter change after MBSR; no task-based fMRI, no emotion regulation task, and no task-related activation results reported. Exclusion IDs: none. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results).

This is a clinical longitudinal study of benign multiple sclerosis with no mention of task-based fMRI, emotion-regulation tasks, or task-related brain activation. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI study), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results). Therefore excluded based on absence of required fMRI emotion-regulation task and outcomes.

Abstract reports task-related fMRI responses to sad faces (task-based, reports activation) in psychiatrically healthy children, but does not clearly state that participants performed an emotion regulation task during scanning. Because I2 (emotion regulation task) is uncertain from the abstract, include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Abstract reports a randomized, placebo-controlled task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in healthy adults and presents task-related activation and functional connectivity results (amygdala and dlPFC). No exclusion criteria are met from the abstract. Full-text review warranted to extract details.

Study is not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I3 (participants in such task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). Thus exclude from this review.

This is a surgical study on total pancreatectomy for IPMT, not an fMRI study of emotion regulation. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI), I2 (not an emotion regulation task), I4 (no task-related brain activation results). I3 (human participants) is irrelevant to the review objective here.

Task-based fMRI in healthy human subjects presenting emotional stimuli with cognitive tasks (self-referential and emotion-labeling). Emotion-labeling constitutes an emotion-regulation/affect-labeling strategy; authors report task-related amygdala activation and condition effects. No exclusion criteria met.

Not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical participants with PPMS). Inclusion NOT met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply. Exclude with high confidence based on abstract alone.

Study is not a task-based fMRI investigation (I1 not met); does not involve emotion regulation or reappraisal tasks (I2 not met); and does not report task-related brain activation (I4 not met). It is an in vivo biochemical study using cerebral microdialysis in surgical patients and therefore outside the review scope. It does involve human participants (I3 met). No exclusion criteria apply (E1,E2 not met).

This is a clinical endocrinology study of adrenalectomy and Nelson's syndrome, not a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation. Inclusion I3 is met (human clinical participants). Inclusion I1, I2, and I4 are not met or not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a structural MRI study of cortical thickness/volume in healthy college students; it is NOT a task-based fMRI study nor does it report task-related activation or an emotion regulation task. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human healthy participants). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion regulation task), I4 (no task-related brain activation reported).

Study is clinical oncology of adult medulloblastoma with no indication of task-based fMRI, emotion regulation task, or task-related brain activation reporting. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation). Exclusion criteria: none met (not a review, not an empathy/perspective-taking study).

Not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). Abstract addresses diagnostic imaging of ampullary tumors, not fMRI or emotion regulation.

Exclusion: study does not involve task-based fMRI or emotion regulation. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply. The paper reports structural neuroradiological MRI in epilepsy, not an emotion-regulation fMRI task.

No task-based fMRI or emotion regulation paradigm reported. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical participants with MS/NMO). Inclusion not met: I1 (task-based fMRI not reported), I2 (emotion regulation/reappraisal task not present), I4 (task-related brain activation results not reported). No exclusion criteria met.

Excluded: study reports structural (white-matter) connectivity in children with disruptive behavior, not a task-based fMRI emotion regulation study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3. Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results).

Study investigates endovascular therapy in acute ischemic stroke patients and MRI angiography-diffusion mismatch; not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criterion I3 (human clinical participants) is satisfied (multiple sclerosis patients). Inclusion criteria I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), and I4 (task-related brain activation results) are not met or not demonstrated in the abstract; study concerns lesion topography for MS diagnosis, not emotion-regulation fMRI.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criterion I3 met (human patients with a separately reported healthy control group). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study — uses DTI/tractography), I2 (no emotion-regulation task; participants did not perform regulation of emotional responses), I4 (no task-related brain activation results). Study is structural DTI only, so excluded.

Task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation (reappraisal) reporting lower prefrontal activation, so I1, I2 and I4 are met. Abstract indicates human UHR participants but does not clearly state a separate control group for the clinical sample, so I3 is not demonstrated; include for full-text review to confirm.

This is a structural MRI/DTI study comparing gray matter volume and FA in children; it is NOT a task-based fMRI study and does not report task-related activation or any emotion regulation task. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion-regulation task), I4 (no task-related brain activation results).

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). The abstract describes a vascular surgery clinical study, not an fMRI emotion-regulation task, so it does not meet the review inclusion criteria.

Task-based fMRI study where human participants used cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate responses to negative pictures; reports task-related neural activation and behavioral effects. Meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract.

Exclusion: none met. Inclusion: none met. Inclusion criteria not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study), I2 (does not involve an emotion regulation task), I4 (no task-related brain activation results reported). I3 (participant/clinical details not relevant to review) also not demonstrated. This is an MRI tumor classification study, not an fMRI emotion-regulation experiment.

Excluded because the study is not a task-based fMRI study (it uses EEG effective-connectivity), so I1 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain/connectivity results). No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in which human participants performed cognitive reappraisal of angry faces (an emotion regulation task) and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity findings. No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the article is a quantitative meta-analysis (E1) and does not present original human task-based fMRI data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 not met (not a primary task-based fMRI study), I2 not demonstrated (no evidence participants performed an emotion-regulation task), I3 not applicable (no original participant sample), I4 not demonstrated (no original task-related activation results reported).

Abstract describes passive emotion perception (viewing multisensory dynamic emotional stimuli) rather than an emotion regulation task; therefore inclusion criterion I2 is not met. It is a task-based fMRI study with healthy participants and reports task-related brain activation (I1, I3, I4 met). No exclusion criteria clearly apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (down-regulation) in N=20 healthy participants and reports task-related brain activation (prefrontal cortex, amygdala) and correlations with working memory capacity and cognitive flexibility. Meets I1-I4. No exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study using a reappraisal emotion-regulation task during scanning with human juvenile participants (clinical offenders and controls) and reports task-related brain activation differences. No exclusion criteria (non-empirical or irrelevant empathy-only tasks) apply.

Study is a task-based fMRI with human participants and reports task-related activation (I1, I3, I4 satisfied). However, participants performed a projective storytelling/perspective-taking AAP task without instructions to regulate emotion, meeting exclusion E2. Inclusion I2 (emotion-regulation task) is not demonstrated.

Exclude because imaging modality is MEG, not task-based fMRI (I1 not met). Abstract does meet I2 (emotion regulation via cognitive reappraisal), I3 (human participants), and I4 (reports task-related neural activation/oscillatory power). No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) are met.

Task-based fMRI study in children/adolescents instructed to up- and down-regulate responses to disgusting images (cognitive reappraisal). Reports task-related brain activation and age-related effects. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans using cognitive reappraisal (decrease negative / increase positive) and reports task-related brain activation results (amygdala, thalamus, midbrain). No exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because I1 (task-based fMRI) is not met: the study used EEG (electrocortical LPP) rather than fMRI. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (human emotion regulation task: distraction and reappraisal), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation via EEG). No exclusion criteria met (E1, E2).

Task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation comparing reappraisal and acceptance in healthy adults; reports task-related BOLD activation and behavioral/autonomic outcomes. Abstract satisfies I1, I2, I3, and I4 with no exclusion criteria met.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that directly tests emotion regulation (reappraisal and suppression) while viewing negative pictures and reports neural activation results, satisfying the review objective and inclusion criteria.

No task-based fMRI or task-related brain activation reported. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human adult clinical participants). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion-regulation task during fMRI), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results).

Abstract reports neuroimaging of emotion processing and regulation in offspring at risk for bipolar disorder but does not specify whether this was a task-based fMRI involving explicit emotion regulation or reporting task-related activation. Human participants are implied. Insufficient detail to confirm I1, I2, and I4, so include for full-text review.

Abstract reports fMRI responses to music listening (not an emotion-regulation task or regulation of responses to visual stimuli). Inclusion met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion not met: I2 (no clear task-based emotion-regulation instruction demonstrated). No exclusion criteria clearly met.

Exclusion: none met. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants) and I4 (reports abnormal task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no evidence participants performed an emotion-regulation task with visual stimuli) and I1 (task-based fMRI not clearly described).

No fMRI data reported: this is an EEG/ERP study, so I1 (task-based fMRI study) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (emotion regulation via cognitive reappraisal), I3 (human participants). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not fMRI), I4 (reports EEG/ERP rather than task-related fMRI activation). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study assessing emotion processing and reappraisal abilities and related brain activity in AUD patients and healthy controls, indicating reappraisal/emotion regulation tasks and reported brain activity; no exclusion criteria met.

Excluding because the study used EEG/ERP (LPP) rather than task-based fMRI, so I1 (task-based fMRI) is not met. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (emotion regulation task), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation via LPP). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (task-based fMRI).

Excluded because the study used PET rather than task-based fMRI (I1 not met). The study involves human participants and reports task-related brain activation (meets I3 and I4). The abstract does not clearly describe an emotion regulation task as defined for inclusion (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met.

Imaging was resting-state (18F-FDG) PET, not task-based fMRI, so I1 is not met. Participants did complete an emotion-regulation task outside the scanner (I2 met) and are human volunteers (I3 met), but the study does not report task-related fMRI activation (I4 not met). No exclusion criteria were met.

Task-based fMRI study in human participants (spider-phobic patients) using cognitive reappraisal as an emotion regulation strategy and reporting fMRI activation related to regulation; fits I1–I4. No exclusion criteria are met in the abstract. Include for full-text review to extract task-related activation details.

Exclude because study used MEG (magnetoencephalography), not task-based fMRI (I1 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (emotion regulation via reappraisal), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation via MEG). Exclusion criteria met: none.

Task-based fMRI study with human participants instructed to use Compassion-meditation and Reappraisal to modulate emotional responses to film clips, and reports task-related brain activation. Thus meets I1,I2,I3,I4. No exclusion criteria are met from the abstract.

EXCLUDED because inclusion criterion I1 (task-based fMRI) is not met: the study used fNIRS, not fMRI. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (emotion regulation/cognitive reappraisal task), I3 (human participants, adults), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results via PFC oxygenation). No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) are met.

No exclusion criteria met (none). Inclusion criteria met: I1, I2, I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not demonstrated: regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli as required by the meta-analysis objective — the study used idiographic sadness/guilt induction (autobiographical recall), not visual stimuli. Therefore excluded.

Abstract reports fMRI connectivity findings in bipolar I disorder (human clinical sample) but does not describe a task-based emotion-regulation or viewing paradigm or report task-related activations. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation).

The abstract describes an empirical task-based fMRI study where 70 youth performed a cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task during fMRI and reports task-related neural activation/variability results related to age and affect. This meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

E1: Non-empirical review/commentary with no original human fMRI data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (human emotion regulation task), I3 (participant group data), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

Exclusion due to not meeting I1: this is an ERP/EEG study (LPP) not a task-based fMRI study. Exclusion criteria met: none (E1, E2 not applicable). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (emotion regulation task: expressive suppression), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation via ERP LPP). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (task-based fMRI study) — therefore excluded from fMRI meta-analysis.

Task-based fMRI with human participants (N=10) performing emotion regulation tasks (reappraisal and affect labeling) and reporting task-related brain activation (amygdala, IFG). Tasks involve regulating emotional responses and fit the meta-analysis objective. No exclusion criteria met.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Study reports resting-state EEG (FAA) correlates of habitual emotion regulation, not task-based fMRI emotion regulation, so excluded.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in human participants examining emotion regulation (instructed reappraisal and uninstructed “respond naturally”) and reports task-related neural activation results (PFC, amygdala). Meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, I4; no exclusion criteria apparent. Include for full-text review.

Excluded because this is a cTBS brain stimulation study and not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met) and it does not report task-related brain activation results (I4 not demonstrated). The study does involve human participants performing an emotion regulation storytelling task (I2) and includes human participants (I3). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation in human participants (depressed patients) and reports prefrontal activation predicting symptom trajectory over 6 months, satisfying I1-I4; no exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI in healthy human participants using attention-to-breath to regulate responses to aversive visual stimuli, with reported task-related brain activation (amygdala and prefrontal cortex) linked to regulation ability. Meets inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports a human study of cognitive reappraisal in younger and older adults (meets I2 and I3). It examines neural correlates, suggesting neuroimaging, but does not explicitly state task-based fMRI or report task-related activation in the abstract. Insufficient detail on imaging modality/results, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI with human younger and older adults employing cognitive reappraisal and selective attention to regulate emotional responses; reports neural connectivity during regulation. This satisfies inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, and I4 and no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract does not describe an emotion regulation task or instructed regulation — it assesses dispositional reappraisal during phobic stimulation (I2 not demonstrated). Inclusion met: I1, I3, I4. No exclusion criteria met.
EXCLUDED because inclusion criterion I1 (task-based fMRI) is not met: the study uses EEG rather than fMRI. Inclusion criteria met: I2, I3, I4. Exclusion criteria met: none (E1, E2 not applicable).

Task-based fMRI with 46 mothers viewing stressful vs. non-stressful child stimuli and reporting task-related brain activation; however the abstract does not state participants were instructed to regulate their emotions, so I2 is uncertain. No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to confirm whether an emotion-regulation instruction/task was used.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human bereaved participants), I4 (task-related activation reported). NOT met: I2 — the study used a numerical Stroop task to assess executive control and reports effects of MBCT, but does not report participants performing an emotion-regulation task (e.g., reappraisal/acceptance instructions during viewing of emotional visual stimuli).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation), reports task-related brain activation results, and involves human participants. The abstract does not specify stimulus modality (visual vs. other), so include for full-text review to confirm stimuli were visual and meet the meta-analysis objective.

Abstract reports a task-based pharmaco-fMRI study in humans using cognitive reappraisal of negative stimuli, with reported task-related activation and connectivity results; no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study with human participants viewing emotion-evoking visual stimuli and reports task-related brain activation differences between groups; meets inclusion criteria for task-based emotion regulation or viewing and reports activations. No exclusion criteria met.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study — uses EEG/LPP), I2 (unclear/does not explicitly instruct emotion regulation), I4 (does not report task-related fMRI activation results). Study therefore excluded from fMRI emotion-regulation meta-analysis.

Study reports task-based fMRI of human participants using a reappraisal (detachment-from-threat) emotion-regulation task and presents reappraisal-related brain activation results (shifts in lateral frontal cortex). Meets inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria apparent.

Abstract reports a task using real-time fMRI (with simultaneous EEG) where participants learned volitional downregulation of amygdala BOLD via neurofeedback, leading to reduced amygdala reactivity to visual stimuli and improved implicit emotion regulation. These findings indicate task-related fMRI activation during an emotion-regulation task. Unclear whether regulation was performed specifically during stimulus presentation, so full-text review is recommended.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in humans using a cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task, reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results, and includes healthy adult participants. All inclusion criteria are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

EXCLUDED because the study used EEG/ERP (LPP) measures rather than task-based fMRI; no fMRI data are reported. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I2 (emotion regulation/cognitive reappraisal frame), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation reported via ERP). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI not demonstrated).

Abstract indicates a neuroimaging study of emotional cue processing but does not specify task-based fMRI, whether participants performed an emotion-regulation or passive viewing task, or report task-related activation results. Information is insufficient to determine whether inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I4 are met. Include for full-text review to clarify methods and outcomes.

Excluded: study used EEG (not task-based fMRI) so I1 not met, and did not involve an instructed emotion-regulation task (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants) and I4 (reports task-related neural activation). No exclusion criteria were met (exclusion_criteria_applied=[]).

Abstract does not indicate participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 not demonstrated). Study is task-based fMRI (I1), includes human participants (I3), and reports task-related activation (I4). No exclusion criteria met.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical sample with controls), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 — participants were exposed to emotional distracters during a cognitive task but were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses (no emotion-regulation task reported).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study with human participants (45 women) who performed explicit reappraisal and an implicit placebo regulation while viewing disgusting visual stimuli; reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results. No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in human participants who decide whether to regulate emotional responses to visual (negative) images; it examines neural predictors and reports task-related brain activation results. This meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are evident.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants, young and older adults), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (no emotion regulation task—participants viewed emotional images but were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses).

No exclusion criteria met. Excluded because the study used EEG/ERPs rather than task-based fMRI (I1 not met). The abstract does meet I2 (human emotion regulation task—positive reappraisal), I3 (human participants), and I4 (reports task-related neural activation results).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal of negative visual scenes that reduced negative affect and reports task-related brain activation (prefrontal cortex, amygdala). This satisfies inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria apply.

EXCLUDED because the study is not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met). The abstract describes an EEG study of cognitive reappraisal (I2 met), with human participants (I3 met) and task-related brain activity reported (EEG; I4 met). No exclusion criteria met.

E2 met: task involved self-/other-referential processing (face-word relevance ratings) with no instruction to amplify or dampen emotion. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participant groups), I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (no evidence of an emotion regulation instruction/strategy).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in human participants examining cognitive reappraisal (instructed and spontaneous) and reports amygdala and prefrontal activation, so it meets inclusion criteria I1–I4. No exclusion criteria are met.

E2: Study examines neural responses/empathy to infant cries without instructions to amplify or dampen emotions (no emotion regulation task). Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human fathers), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no emotion-regulation instructions or task).

E1: This is a review article summarizing neuroimaging studies rather than reporting original human task-based fMRI data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI study reporting original data), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), I3 (participant groups with original data), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

Include for full-text review: Abstract reports an RCT assessing clinical and neurobiological changes in humans (I3 satisfied) but does not specify use of task-based fMRI, an emotion-regulation task, or task-related activation results (I1, I2, I4 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text required to determine whether task-based emotion-regulation fMRI data are reported.

EXCLUDED: This is a genome-wide association genetics study with no fMRI, no task-based emotion regulation, and no task-related brain activation results. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs NOT met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results).

This is a task-based fMRI study with human participants instructed to increase or decrease their affective responses to visual images. The abstract reports task-related brain activation results. All inclusion criteria (I1–I4) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract reports human participants with social anxiety and neural/behavioral responses but does not specify that tasks were fMRI-based or involved explicit emotion regulation (or pure viewing), nor does it state task-related brain activation results. Key eligibility (I1, I2, I4) cannot be confirmed from abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Longitudinal task-based fMRI where adults performed effortful emotion regulation of negative stimuli; reports task-related activation (amygdala, ventrolateral/dorsolateral PFC). Meets I1-I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met): the study measured EEG theta oscillations during distraction while viewing pictures. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (adolescents performed an emotion-regulation/distraction task), I3 (human participants, adolescents and young adults), I4 (reports task-related brain activation measures via EEG). No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) apply.

Study used diffusion tensor imaging (structural MRI) and self-report measures, not task-based fMRI; participants did not perform an emotion regulation task during scanning and no task-related activation results are reported. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results).

Excluded because the study used fNIRS rather than task-based fMRI and did not employ an instructed emotion-regulation paradigm. No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (task-based fMRI absent) and I2 (no instructed emotion-regulation task).
Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study with human participants that includes an explicit emotion regulation task (reappraisal) and reports brain activation results; no exclusion criteria are met.

E1: The paper is a theoretical/review article presenting an argument and literature review, not original human fMRI data. E1 applies: this is a non-empirical review article without original human data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study), I2 (no participants performing an emotion regulation task), I3 (no participant groups reported in original data), I4 (no original task-related activation results reported).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (distancing) in healthy human participants and presents task-related brain activation results (ventral striatum, fronto-parietal network). No exclusion criteria are met.

Study used EEG (LPP) and facial EMG, not task-based fMRI; thus I1 (task-based fMRI) is not met. Inclusion met: I2 (emotion regulation task), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation via LPPs). No exclusion criteria applied.

Exclusion: none. Inclusion met: I3 (human parent-child participants). Inclusion not met: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study; uses fNIRS hyperscanning), I2 (not an instructed emotion-regulation task like reappraisal), I4 (does not report task-related fMRI activation results).

EXCLUDE because I1 not met: study used EEG (not task-based fMRI). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I3 (human adult participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results via EEG). Exclusion criteria met: none (E1,E2 not applicable).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I2 (not an emotion regulation task — participants passively heard/emoted to vocal words; also stimuli are auditory, not visual, so it does not address the review objective).

Abstract reports a resting-state/physiological fMRI study of respiration and heart-rate oscillations, not a task-based emotion-regulation experiment. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) apply.

Task-based fMRI study of negative face processing in >500 young adults reporting task-related amygdala activation, habituation, and amygdala–vmPFC connectivity. Although no explicit regulation instructions are described, the review accepts studies that view emotional stimuli without regulating; thus inclusion criteria I1–I4 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

EXCLUDED because this is an ERP/EEG study, not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met), and it does not involve instructed emotion regulation (I2 not met). It reports human participants and task-related neural responses (I3 and I4 met). No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) apply.

Task-based fMRI with human participants instructed to regulate responses to visual food stimuli using cognitive reappraisal, suppression and up-/down-regulation; reports task-related brain activation results. Fits meta-analysis objective of regulation of emotional/affective responses to visual stimuli.

E1 applies — abstract appears to be a narrative/review without original human task-fMRI data. No evidence of I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (human participants performing an emotion-regulation task), I3 (participant details), or I4 (task-related brain activation results). Exclude based on lack of empirical task-fMRI data.

No task-based fMRI or emotion-regulation task reported. Study uses proton chemical shift imaging in developmental stuttering (metabolic/neuroimaging), not task-related fMRI activation. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met (E1,E2).

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human adolescent participants). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). The study reports resting-state functional connectivity rather than a task-based emotion regulation paradigm, so it does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

Study uses EEG/ERP, not task-based fMRI (I1 not met), and does not instruct participants to regulate their emotion (no emotion regulation task; I2 not met). It includes human children (I3 met) and reports task-related brain activity via ERPs (I4 met). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

Exclusion met: E1 (review article without original human data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not an original task-based fMRI study), I2 (no evidence participants performed an emotion regulation task), I3 (no participant groups reported), I4 (no task-related activation results reported). Therefore excluded based on being a non-empirical review.

Excluded because the study does not involve an emotion regulation task (I2 not met). It is a task-based fMRI study with healthy human participants and reports task-related activation (I1, I3, I4 met). No exclusion criteria apply.

No evidence in abstract of a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm or task-related activation results. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results), I3 (participant sample not specified in abstract).

Excluded because abstract does not describe an emotion regulation task (I2 not met): the study examines decision-induced rationalization without instructions to regulate emotional responses. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activations). No exclusion criteria met.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants reported), I4 (reports task-related brain activation — ERP). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not task-based fMRI; EEG/ERP study), I2 (not an emotion-regulation task).

Abstract does not report task-based fMRI or task-related brain activation results (I1 and I4 not met). It does involve human participants performing instructed emotion regulation (I2) and a human sample (I3). No exclusion criteria appear met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of human participants performing emotion regulation of negative visual stimuli, examining SSRI effects and 5-HTTLPR moderation and reporting neural (fMRI) outcomes. This meets the review’s task, participant, and activation-report criteria. No exclusion criteria are indicated in the abstract.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI; participants performed effortful emotion regulation (emotional faces n-back assessing voluntary attentional control); includes schizophrenia patients with matched healthy controls reported separately; reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study with adolescent human participants and task-related brain activation (I1, I3, I4). It does not clearly state participants were instructed to regulate emotion (I2 unclear); observed 'emotion regulation and mentalizing' may be spontaneous. No exclusion criterion is clearly met. Include for full-text review to determine whether an instructed emotion-regulation task was used or E2 applies.

E1: Non-empirical review without original human data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI study), I2 (human participants performing an emotion regulation task), I3 (original human participants reported), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results).

Excluded: study used EEG/ERP (LPP), not task-based fMRI, so I1 not met. It did not involve an instructed emotion regulation strategy (participants viewed pictures while performing math), so I2 not met. It does not report task-related fMRI activation results (I4 not met). It does include human participants (I3 met). No exclusion criteria were triggered.

E2 met: study is an empathy/perspective-taking task without instructions to amplify or dampen participants' emotional responses. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation results). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not an fMRI study; used fNIRS) and I2 (not an emotion-regulation task).

Exclusion based on failure to meet inclusion criteria: Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study; uses resting-state fMRI), I2 (no emotion regulation task during scanning), I4 (no task-related activation results reported; reports resting-state connectivity changes).

Task-based BOLD fMRI in healthy adults randomized to compassion vs reappraisal training; participants engaged in instructed emotion-regulation strategies while viewing suffering/non-suffering images; reports task-related neural activation (amygdala, insula, OFC). No exclusion criteria met.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion I3 met (human children sample). Inclusion I1 not met: this is EEG/ERP study, not a task-based fMRI study required by the review. Inclusion I2 not demonstrated: placebo manipulation is not an instructed emotion-regulation task (e.g., reappraisal). Inclusion I4 not met for fMRI brain-activation reporting (EEG/ERP reported instead). Therefore excluded.

EXCLUDE because this is a structural MRI study of trait expressive suppression, not a task-based fMRI emotion regulation experiment. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human healthy participants). Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI study), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (emotion regulation task: instructed suppression), I3 (human healthy adult participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation via ERP LPP). Inclusion criterion not met: I1 — study used EEG/ERP (LPP), not task-based fMRI, so it does not meet the meta-analysis modality requirement.

No fMRI data and not an emotion regulation task: study uses EEG/ERN measures of error processing, not task-based fMRI, and does not involve regulating emotional responses. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation via EEG). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task).

This is an annual research review (non-empirical); no original human task-based fMRI data are reported. Exclusion E1 applies. None of the inclusion criteria (I1-I4) are demonstrated in the abstract: no task-based fMRI, no emotion-regulation task, no participant data, and no task-related activation results.

I2 not met: the task involves sadness introspection and judging nonemotional features, but participants were not instructed to regulate (e.g., reappraise, amplify, or dampen) their emotional responses. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human adolescent sample), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Exclusion met: none (E1 and E2 not applicable). Therefore exclude due to failure to meet I2 (emotion regulation task).

Abstract does not describe a task-based emotion regulation fMRI study. It reports network analyses of functional interactions (likely resting-state or non-regulation task), with no mention of regulating or viewing emotional visual stimuli or task-related activation. Inclusion met: I3 (older adult human participants). Inclusion not met: I1, I2, I4. Exclusion criteria: none met.
Task-based fMRI study where human participants performed cognitive reappraisal of positive and negative visual images and reported task-related brain activation results; clearly meets I1–I4.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activations). Inclusion criterion not met: I2 — the study examines generation/regulation of internally generated emotions, not regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli or viewing stimuli as required by the meta-analysis objective.

Exclusion: none met. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants implied). Inclusion not met: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study; resting-state fMRI), I2 (not an emotion regulation task; measures dispositional optimism at rest), I4 (does not report task-related brain activation). Therefore excluded from this meta-analysis focused on task-based emotion regulation fMRI.

Included for full-text review. Abstract reports a human (women with PTSD) neuroimaging study of emotional processing, but it does not specify whether a task-based emotion-regulation paradigm was used, whether task-related activation results are reported, or whether a control group is included. I1, I2, and I4 are not demonstrated in the abstract. No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met: I1 (not task-based fMRI; uses resting-state fNIRS), I2 (not an emotion regulation task; stress induction/rumination measure), I4 (does not report task-related brain activation). Therefore excluded based on failure to meet required inclusion criteria.

E2 applies: This is an empathy/vicarious-pain study without instructions to amplify or dampen participants' emotional responses, so it does not meet the emotion-regulation requirement. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (emotion regulation task).

Excluded because the study reports structural (grey matter volume) associations with habitual reappraisal rather than task-based fMRI activation. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (task-based fMRI) not met; I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task) not demonstrated; I4 (reports task-related brain activation results) not met. No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) are met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal emotion regulation task in human participants and presents task-related brain activation results (vmPFC tracking of subjective and normative valence). No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded (E2): This is a task-based fMRI study (I1) with human participants (I3) reporting task-related activations (I4), but it measures mentalizing/perspective-taking without instruction to alter participants' emotional responses—fits exclusion E2; I2 (emotion-regulation task) not met or demonstrated.

Not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met) and does not report an emotion regulation task (I2 not met). It does involve human participants (I3) and reports task-related neural activation via ERPs (I4). No exclusion criteria met. Exclude for full-text review because the modality and task do not match the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs clearly met: I2 (emotion regulation via distraction) and I4 (task-related brain activation reported via oxyHb changes). (c) Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 is not met — study used NIRS, not task-based fMRI; I3 not clearly demonstrated (participant details not specified). Therefore excluded due to I1 not met.

Animal histological study of lamprey brain using PCNA; not a human task-based fMRI emotion regulation study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs NOT met: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (no human emotion regulation task), I3 (not human participants), I4 (no task-related fMRI activation results).

Not an fMRI emotion-regulation study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants implied by EEG/EEG on scalp). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (not an emotion-regulation task), I4 (reports EEG evoked potentials, not task-related fMRI activation results).

This is an animal (macaque) anatomical tracer study, not a human task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation. Does not meet inclusion criteria I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (human emotion regulation task), I3 (human participants), or I4 (task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria clearly met.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI not clearly reported), I2 (no emotion regulation task described), I4 (no task-related activation results reported). Abstract describes parental brain connectivity to infant stimuli and longitudinal child outcomes, not an emotion-regulation fMRI task.

Excluded: No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I3 (healthy human participants). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study; this is EEG), I2 (no emotion-regulation task; study examines attentional control without regulation of emotional responses), I4 (does not report task-related fMRI activation results).

Not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met) and does not involve instructed emotion regulation (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation via EEG). No exclusion criteria met (E1,E2).

This is a theoretical/hypothesis paper without original human data (E1). It does not report task-based fMRI (I1), emotion-regulation tasks (I2), participant groups (I3), or task-related brain activation results (I4).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (not human participants performing emotion regulation; study used pigs with olfactory stimulation rather than human emotion-regulation tasks) and I3 (non-human subjects; human participant requirement not satisfied). Therefore excluded based on non-human animal study and lack of an emotion-regulation task in humans.

Task-based fMRI study measuring BOLD responses to unpleasant (sport-specific and general) images in athletes and controls; reports task-related activation (prefrontal cortex, insula). Abstract does not state explicit emotion-regulation instructions, so inclusion on regulation criterion is unclear; include for full-text review to determine whether regulation or passive viewing was used.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in human (BPD) participants examining neural correlates of provocation-focused rumination, but does not specify that participants regulated emotional responses to visual stimuli or used standard emotion-regulation instructions (e.g., reappraisal). Eligibility for the meta-analysis is therefore uncertain from the abstract and warrants full-text review.

EXCLUDED: This is an EEG study of motor processing in adolescents, not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met). It does not investigate emotion regulation of visual stimuli (I2 not met) and does not report fMRI task-related activation (I4 not met). It does involve human participants (I3 met). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

Study uses EEG/ERP (N2) and source-estimated ROIs, not task-based fMRI, so I1 (task-based fMRI) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (emotion regulation task), I3 (human children participants), I4 (task-related brain activation reported). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract describes behavioral eye-tracking with self-report; no fMRI or brain-activation results reported. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (cognitive reappraisal task), I3 (human participants). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation results).

Task-based fMRI with human participants viewing religious vs nonreligious images during painful stimulation; contemplation of the religious image led to emotional detachment (an emotion-regulation-like process) and the paper reports task-related brain activations (right VLPFC). Fits inclusion criteria for emotion regulation to visual stimuli and reports brain activation results.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in healthy human participants, with voxelwise task-related brain activation results (PFC and amygdala). This satisfies inclusion criteria I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Study is excluded because it does not address the review objective: participants regulated emotion during autobiographical memory recall rather than in response to visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation via cognitive reappraisal), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activation). No exclusion criteria met (none).

Abstract provides insufficient methodological detail to determine whether this is a task-based fMRI study reporting task-related activation during an emotion regulation task. Title suggests neural measures of emotion regulation, but inclusion criteria I1–I4 are not demonstrated in the abstract. Include for full-text review to confirm whether task-based fMRI and task activation results are reported.

No evidence the task involved active emotion regulation. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human adolescent clinical sample with NSSI), I4 (reports neural responses to emotional stimuli). Inclusion not met: I2 — study examined automatic processing of masked emotional faces with no instruction to regulate emotions. Exclusion criteria: none (E1,E2 not met).

Excluded because study used fNIRS (not task-based fMRI) and did not involve an emotion regulation instruction. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (not fMRI—used fNIRS), I2 (no emotion regulation task—participants judged emotion/speed rather than regulating their emotions).

Event-related fMRI study with human participants doing a voluntary emotion regulation task (maintain vs passively view negative/neutral pictures) and reporting task-related amygdala activation; meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apparent.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study where human participants used cognitive reappraisal to regulate cravings (personal-food images), and reports task-related neural activation (frontoparietal network, multivariate analyses). No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in humans performing cognitive emotion regulation (CER) during aversive visual processing and reports task-related brain activation/network results; no exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to extract detailed contrasts and participants.

Study is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting task-related activation (meets I1, I3, I4) but does not involve an emotion-regulation task with visual stimuli or instruction to regulate affect (does not meet I2). No exclusion criteria are triggered (none of E1–E2 apply).

Task-based fMRI study (N=26) of primiparous mothers using distraction to regulate emotions in response to infant crying; reports reduced amygdala activation with regulation. Satisfies I1,I2,I3,I4. Stimulus modality appears auditory (infant crying) not visual, so relevance to the visual-stimulus meta-analysis objective is uncertain; include for full-text review.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI reported in Study 2), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I2 (no emotion regulation task—participants were not instructed to regulate; study measured passive/individual differences in responses to fear-eliciting stimuli). Therefore excluded because I2 is not satisfied.

Abstract provides insufficient information to confirm task-based fMRI, specific emotion regulation task, visual stimuli, or reported brain activation. Include for full-text review to determine if inclusion criteria I1–I4 are met.

No evidence in abstract of a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm. The study reports pre/post EEG-neurofeedback amygdala connectivity (likely resting/connectivity analysis), not regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli. Human PTSD patients are studied, but task-based activation/results are not demonstrated.

No emotion-regulation task of visual stimuli was used: the study used an arithmetic task with auditory feedback measuring distress tolerance, not instructed cognitive reappraisal or similar. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion IDs not met: I2 (no emotion-regulation task as defined).

Task-based fMRI with human adults using instructed emotion regulation (increase/decrease negative responses) during a task; reports ACC activation and connectivity related to errors (task-related brain activation). Fits inclusion criteria I1-I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in human adolescents during an emotion regulation task (including passive viewing of negative vs neutral visual stimuli) and reports task-related vmPFC–amygdala functional connectivity linked to psychopathology, matching the review objective and inclusion criteria.

Study uses implicit emotional processing (gender judgment) without instructions to regulate emotion. Exclusion IDs met: []. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical and control groups), I4 (reports task-related task activation/connectivity). Inclusion IDs not met: I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task).

Abstract reports passive viewing of fearful faces and correlational analyses with trait optimism, not an instructed emotion-regulation task. Meets I1, I3, I4 (task-based fMRI; older adult human sample; reports task-related activation). Does NOT demonstrate I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task). No exclusion criteria met.

Study is a task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive reappraisal in human participants (69 female adults), reporting task-related brain activation correlated with real-life affect. It meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are apparent from the abstract.

Excluded (E2): study examines empathy for others' pain without instructions to amplify or dampen participants' emotional responses. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related activation results). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I2 (no explicit emotion-regulation instruction such as reappraisal/perspective-taking to alter affect).

EXCLUDED (E1): This is a literature reappraisal/review of cluster-like headache case reports without original task-based fMRI data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study), I2 (does not involve an emotion regulation task), I3 (no participants performing such tasks reported), I4 (no task-related brain activation results).

Task-based real-time fMRI neurofeedback study in human adolescents (7–16) teaching up-/down-regulation of an emotion-regulation region (insula); reports task-related activation and connectivity. Unclear whether regulation targeted emotional responses to visual stimuli specifically, but meets broad emotion-regulation criteria and warrants full-text review.

E1: This is a review/non-empirical paper (‘We review the research...’) and does not report original task-based fMRI data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study), I2 (no emotion-regulation task with participants), I3 (no original participant group reported as data), I4 (no task-related brain activation results).

Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study), I2 (no emotion regulation task reported), I4 (no task-related brain activation results). This is a structural VBM study correlating gray matter volume with personality traits (disgust sensitivity), not task-based fMRI of emotion regulation.

Study reports a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy human (female) participants performing voluntary emotion regulation of emotional pictures and reports task-related brain activation results; matches I1, I2, I3, and I4. No exclusion criteria met.

E1 met: this paper is a systematic review summarizing imaging studies and does not present original human task-based fMRI data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI data not reported in this paper), I2 (no evidence participants performed an emotion-regulation task), I3 (no original participant groups reported), I4 (no task-related activation results presented).

Abstract describes a genetic/behavioral study of emotion regulation tendencies, not a task-based fMRI study and it does not report task-related brain activation results. Human participants are included. Excluding because I1 and I4 are not met; I3 is met.

Abstract reports a film-based emotion reactivity and regulation task performed in an MRI scanner, with age-related changes in emotional reactivity and reported brain activation (middle frontal gyrus). Fits task-based fMRI emotion regulation studies; no exclusion criteria met.

This is explicitly a review article examining models and prior fMRI findings, not an empirical study with original human data (meets exclusion E1). The abstract does not report original task-based fMRI methods, participants, or new task-related activation results, so inclusion criteria I1-I4 are not met or demonstrated.

Excluded because the study uses resting-state fMRI pre/post an emotion provocation, not task-based fMRI or an explicit emotion-regulation instruction. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants with offender and control groups). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study during regulation), I2 (no explicit emotion-regulation task described), I4 (no task-related activation reported; only resting-state connectivity). Exclusion criteria met: none [].

Task-based fMRI with human participants and reports task-related brain activation (I1, I3, I4). Include for full-text review to determine whether the task fits the review's emotion-regulation definition.

Excluded because inclusion criterion I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task) is not met: the task manipulated cognitive conflict and did not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses. No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I2.

Task-based fMRI in 40 healthy human participants viewing emotion-eliciting images while applying emotion regulation strategies (goal vs. implementation intentions). No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion I2 not met: this study examines pain control/relief during thermal stimulation, not emotion regulation of visual stimuli or instructions to regulate emotional responses. Therefore excluded for not addressing the review objective.

E2: This is an empathy-for-pain study with no evidence participants were instructed to amplify or dampen their emotional response (no emotion-regulation task described). Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activations). Inclusion not met: I2 (no indication of an emotion-regulation instruction; dlPFC interpretation is observational).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (clinical human participants implied). Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study), I2 (does not involve an emotion-regulation task), I4 (does not report task-related brain activation). Not an emotion-regulation task: abstract describes reading narratives with associated brain activation but no instruction to regulate emotion (I2 not met). No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: none. Task-based fMRI emotional face-processing study reporting task-related amygdala activation/habituation in human adolescents. Excluded (E1): This is a theoretical/review article without original human data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study), I2 (no emotion-regulation task reported), I4 (no task-related brain activation results); I3 not addressed.

Excluded because the study investigates reward-persistence and valuation, not emotion regulation of visual stimuli. Exclusion IDs met: []. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activations). Study uses resting-state fMRI (tonic connectivity) rather than a task-based emotion-regulation paradigm. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical participants). Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Task-based fMRI study with healthy human participants performing neurofeedback to regulate amygdala responses to negative pictures (broadly defined emotion regulation). E1 met: this is a rationale/design/methods (protocol) paper without reported original task-based fMRI results. Excluded: Study does not involve emotion regulation or viewing emotional stimuli; it investigates motor planning and control. Task-based fMRI in adolescents/young adults reporting rVLPFC activation to negative emotional words and links to emotion reappraisal and alcohol use. Task-based fMRI using an emotion-word Stroop with emotional distractors; examines cognitive control of emotion in presence of affective stimuli and reports task-related brain activation in human adults. No task-based fMRI or task-related activation reported; study is structural (gray matter volume) correlational work in healthy humans. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1, I2, I4. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract describes a task-based rt-fMRI study in healthy human participants who performed an emotion regulation task (down-regulation) while viewing aversive visual stimuli; it reports ROI and whole-brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review.

Task-based event-related fMRI study examining cognitive distraction as an anticipatory emotion regulation strategy; reports task-related brain activation (mPFC, amygdala) in human participants. Meets I1-I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study examining neural responses to threat cues during partner/stranger/no-handholding and reports threat-related brain activity, but it is unclear whether participants were instructed to perform an emotion regulation task (social support may be implicit). Task-based fMRI with an intentional empathy (perspective-taking) task, healthy human subjects, and task-related hemodynamic activation reported. Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans (older adults) who performed an emotion-regulation task (increase/decrease responses to negative pictures, i.e., reappraisal/ regulation), and presents task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met in the abstract.

Human task-based rtfMRI study reporting task-related activation and voluntary modulation of emotional states via neurofeedback. No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants measured).
